newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Peregrine Inv upbeat on 1997 prospects.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine Inv upbeat on 1997 prospects.

text.p: Asian investment bank Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it was optimistic about prospects for 1997 despite weakness in some Asian capital markets.

Excluding exceptionals, the Hong Kong-based investment bank's core profits had grown in 1996, said Peregrine chairman Philip Tose, unveiling a net profit to December 31 of HK$856 million, down from HK$1.01 billion in the previous year.

"If we were comparing apples with apples, group operating profits before taxation and exceptional items have risen to about US$110 million, against US$31 million last year," Tose told a news conference.
"In Hong Kong dollar terms that's HK$849 million against HK$238 million," Tose said.
The previous year's net profits were swelled by an exceptional gain from the sale of a majority stake in INVESCO Plc.
If not for weakness in capital markets in Korea, Thailand and India in 1996, which all hit three-year lows, the group would have also seen "quite a large increase in revenue", Tose said.
Tose said the Hong Kong-based investment bank's decision to leave the total dividend at HK$0.53 for 1996, unchanged from the previous total dividend, reflected its optimism about 1997 prospects.

"We believe that 1997 should be a relatively satisfactory year," Tose said. "If we were not so confident, particularly at this stage of the year, I think we would definitely have cut the dividend back."
Peregrine Investments is a Hong Kong-based financial institution engaged in securities dealing and property investment.
Tose admitted that the group's asset management arm had lost money.
"This we expected," Tose said. "It's still going very much according to plan. We believe that this is a five-year programme and we're just really in the second year of that programme."
Peregrine's fixed income arm had done well, lifting operating profits before taxation to HK$381.5 million, from HK$158.22 million in 1995.

Its 50.14 percent subsidiary, investment holding and property development company Kwong Sang Hong International Ltd reported on Tuesday that net profits for the year to December 31 totalled HK$202 million, up from HK$155 million in 1995.
